title: Terminal
summary: A Terminal is a Node on the Canvas with your own shell in it; agents do not use it. In a zsh Terminal, Terminal AI, help from a Claude model, proposes text for your input line.

scene.description: The Terminal in worfy. On the Canvas lies a Terminal Node. Its shell starts in the Project folder; your keys go to the shell, and its output comes back to the Node. Another screen, a window or a Linked machine, opens the same shell. In zsh, the shell sends the typed line to Terminal AI and gets grey text back; Fix in the Node's header asks Terminal AI too. Terminal AI asks Claude Code, which reports the Limits, and the Limits may pause Terminal AI.

labels.terminalNote: your shell; agents do not use it
labels.otherNote: a window or a Linked machine
labels.terminalAiNote: zsh only; never runs a command
labels.claudeNote: one turn per request, no tools
labels.step1: New terminal in the Canvas menu creates the Node. Its shell starts in the Project folder: your login shell on macOS, PowerShell or Git Bash on Windows.
labels.step2: The shell keeps running when the Node scrolls out of sight or the window reloads, and the next view redraws its last output. Closing the Node ends the shell.
labels.step3: Other windows, and a Linked machine with write access, show the same shell and may type in it. The screen that typed or clicked last sets its size.
labels.step4: In a zsh Terminal, Terminal AI shows grey text after the cursor, from your history or from Claude. → takes it; Enter stays with you.
labels.step5: After a failed command, Fix in the Node's header asks Claude for a corrected command and puts it into the line. Near the Limits, Terminal AI pauses until the window resets.

flow.description: The data flow of a Terminal. In the renderer: the Terminal Node. In the main process: the TerminalRegistry, the ReplayBuffer, the headless screen, ShellLink and AssistService. The processes: the shell in node-pty and Claude Code. The Node opens the shell with terminal.open and sends keys on terminal.input; the registry writes them to the shell. Each chunk of output goes to the ReplayBuffer, to the headless screen and to the Node on terminal.output. The headless screen answers a program's questions to the shell. A zsh sends an ask over a Unix socket to ShellLink, which passes it to AssistService; the service asks Claude Code for one turn, and ShellLink sends show or insert back to the shell. Fix starts at the Node with terminalAi.fix.run.

labels.shellLinkNote: routes an ask to its function

text: main owns each shell and a view only draws it, so a shell outlives its view and several screens share one. The renderer names a Project and a Node, never a folder or a program.

In zsh, worfy's script marks each prompt and command with OSC 633 sequences and a nonce that programs do not know. Terminal AI is not a Session: its Claude Code process has no tools and no transcript.

limits: A Terminal keeps the last 256 KB of output for the next view, and a view keeps 5000 lines of scrollback.
Terminal AI gives up after 5 s for a Suggestion, 8 s for Next command and 30 s for Command request and Fix.
Suggestion and Next command pause above 80 % of the 5-hour window or on a Limits warning; Command request and Fix only when the Limits reject.
